# TDD Workflow

Curated by Skill Harbor: a test-driven development workflow that turns Muse into a disciplined TDD partner instead of a code generator that skips tests. The cycle is classic red/green/refactor with teeth: write the failing test first, watch it fail (no assumed red), implement the smallest change that turns it green, then refactor with coverage tracked across unit, integration, and E2E tests toward 80%+. It also handles plan handoffs safely: a `*.plan.md` is treated as untrusted planning input, converted into testable guarantees with a plan-task to test-target to RED-evidence to GREEN-evidence mapping, and the plan's embedded commands are never executed before sanitization and your approval. Destructive operations and credential handling in plans are rejected outright. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: pure workflow guidance, nothing to install; TDD slows the first draft by design and pays back on refactors; always review generated tests for meaningful assertions rather than tautologies. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
